record.original_question: Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, µ, S), a number of colors r, and a threshold λ in the measure range, calculate the (r, λ)-centerpole number c_r^λ(X), meaning the smallest size of a subfamily S' ⊂ S such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a monochromatic S'-symmetric measurable set of measure at least λ.

evidence.quote: A subfamily S′ ⊂ S will be called (r, λ)-centerpole if for any measurable r-coloring of X there is a monochromatic S′-symmetric subset A ∈ dom(µ) of measure µ(A) ≥ λ. The minimal cardinality |S′| of a (r, λ)-centerpole subset S′ ⊂ S will be denoted by cλr (X) and called the (r, λ)-centerpole number of X.
Problem 10.1. Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, µ, S) calculate its (r, λ)-centerpole numbers cλr (X).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A symmetry measure space is a triple X = (X, μ, S), where (X, μ) is a measure space with σ-algebra dom(μ), and S is a family of involutions (or, more generally, transformations) of X each of which is measurable and measure-preserving. A subset A ∈ dom(μ) is called S'-symmetric, for a subfamily S' ⊂ S, if there exists s ∈ S' with s(A) = A. A measurable r-coloring of X is a partition X = C_1 ∪ ... ∪ C_r into r measurable pieces.

Fix an integer r ≥ 1 and a real number λ in the range of μ. A subfamily S' ⊂ S is called (r, λ)-centerpole if for every measurable r-coloring of X there exist an index i ∈ {1,...,r} and a measurable S'-symmetric subset A ⊂ C_i with μ(A) ≥ λ. Define the (r, λ)-centerpole number
   c_r^λ(X) := min{ |S'| : S' ⊂ S is (r, λ)-centerpole }.

Problem. Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, μ, S), determine (compute or give sharp bounds for) the (r, λ)-centerpole numbers c_r^λ(X) for all admissible parameters r and λ.
artifact.status_search_result: The centerpole number framework, introduced in the Ramsey-theoretic study of symmetry on measure spaces by Banakh and collaborators, is posed as a general computation problem. No general formula appears in the literature; only specific cases (e.g., particular groups, intervals, or geometric figures) have been treated. The general problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: ms(Ω, r) is the maximum m such that for any r-coloring of Ω there exists a monochromatic symmetric set of size at least m, considered for various specific spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific instances of the symmetric-Ramsey/centerpole problem have been computed; the general problem remains a research direction.

status_evidence.title: Banakh spaces and their geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to develop the geometry related to Banakh's symmetry framework.
status_evidence.claim: Active follow-up research suggests the general centerpole number problem has not been resolved.
